blocks.6c9539fc724a: Build from source. Requirements: Node 24.x (the repository pins 24.15.0), Corepack with pnpm 11.16.0, Git, and at least one harness on PATH. Linux also needs build-essential and python3; macOS needs Xcode Command Line Tools.
blocks.744849a85eae: A new session starts on its own branch at the current HEAD, so two agents in the same repository never edit the same checkout. Sleep a direct session to stop the process while keeping the checkout and resume token; wake it to continue where the harness supports it.
blocks.7515956b0c2e: Prefer the terminal? Meet iCode Agent
blocks.78c3db47141d: iCode Workbench · Open-source agent development environment
blocks.87243de9ad8d: Recurring work joins the same queue.
blocks.8dd8cc3d0552: Schedules create ordinary queued tasks on a cadence — once, daily, weekdays, weekly, or every few hours — with queue-or-skip overlap handling and run-now. Pausing a schedule leaves tasks already created untouched, and every occurrence lands in the same task queue as work you queued by hand.
blocks.909728574b86: Open Files beside the terminal and work in the same worktree the agent is editing. Explore, rename, duplicate, move, and search; Monaco adds editing, quick diffs against HEAD, inline blame, and file history.
blocks.986ff6764ea4: iCode Workbench runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and 40+ more CLI agents in parallel, each in its own Git worktree. Queue durable tasks, review changes where the agent worked, manage any session from its own row, and keep terminals alive when the app restarts — while Mira watches every repository and tells you what needs you.
blocks.a037c51e9808: A real PTY in the session worktree; the detached host keeps it alive. The terminal follows the app appearance, with a light ANSI palette on the light canvas.
blocks.a09412a7fbd4: iCode Workbench is pre-1.0 and ships as an unsigned build. CI produces Linux x64, Windows x64, and macOS x64 / arm64 packages for every tagged release, and the installers are published on GitHub Releases. Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper warn on first launch; on macOS, right-click the app and choose Open. The source is public under AGPL-3.0-only, and a modified version offered to users over a network must provide them the corresponding source.
blocks.a15fd33ab133: The task workbench: the instruction, the session, changes against the baseline, and a review decision.
blocks.af83e4e23e49: Details, sleep or wake, restart, pin, and remove are one right-click away. Lifecycle actions target the row's session even when another session is on screen, and an unavailable action explains why. If uncommitted or unmerged work is at risk, removal names the files or the retained branch and keeps the branch — there is no name to copy or type.
blocks.b1405d0d4fdb: Tasks are supervised, not autonomous: a permission prompt still waits for a person.
blocks.bbf891b0d3b6: Every session gets its own worktree.
blocks.c954006a9209: Pinned projects, direct sessions grouped by worktree, the cross-project task queue, and live counts share one sidebar. Every row opens its own menu: a session row carries details, sleep or wake, restart, pin, and remove without switching to it first.
blocks.cca2e271a79f: She comes to you. Approvals, failures, waiting tasks, and review-ready work become proactive messages with a sidebar badge and an OS notification when no window is focused. Deduplication, an hourly budget, and quiet hours keep it from becoming noise.
blocks.dd6fc7017d7f: Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode get native provider injection and Mira's native conversation. 21 harnesses have managed status hooks. 44 are launchable — from GitHub Copilot and Gemini to Cursor, Cline, Aider, Goose, Qwen Code, and more.
blocks.de75dcb63e1f: Mira reads the real queue: review-ready work, running sessions, and uncommitted changes.
blocks.df081c698e5f: She is bounded. She has no shell and no project working directory. She cannot approve a proposal, decide a review, merge, push, or edit project code.
blocks.e297649b1b1b: She can act. Through validated actions she creates, cancels, retries, and archives tasks, messages task sessions and project supervisors, and records non-binding review recommendations.
blocks.e2e09ee7e692: Mira is a person in the sidebar, not another project tab. One conversation spans every repository, and her answers come from the real projects, tasks, sessions, diffs, and review state.
blocks.e7ba3856316a: Then choose Add project, start a session, queue a task, or open Mira and ask what needs you.
blocks.ec5f9d4b6940: A control room for a fleet of CLI agents.
blocks.f49b511b6223: Files, Search, and Source Control share the persistent inspector, and the task workbench gives Files and Source Control full-width tabs. Changes are scoped to the session checkout: stage, inspect inline diffs, send line notes back to the agent, and commit, amend, push, cherry-pick, revert, or reset.
blocks.f7514442a12c: Schedules are in-process timers and need iCode Workbench running.
